SECTION 1 — PURPOSE OF THE RESEARCH This study compares two methods of undergraduate chemistry instruction: • Group A — Virtual Reality (VR): Using a Meta Quest 3 head -mounted display (HMD) to complete virtual chemistry simulations. Absolutely ZERO real chemicals are involved at any point. • Group B — Traditional Physical Laboratory: Attending a supervised lab session with real equipment, a live Bunsen burner flame exceeding 1,000°C, and real chemical solutions. Both groups complete the same two experiments — a Flame Test for metal ion identification and an Acid –Base Identification procedure — then a short knowledge quiz and an anonymous Likert survey. This is an undergraduate Computer Science honours thesis at Al goma University. In rare cases, these can trigger seizures or epileptic episodes in susceptible individuals. YOU MUST NOT PARTICIPATE IN THE VR GROUP IF YOU HAVE: epilepsy, a history of seizures, photosensitive epilepsy, photosensitivity disorder, or any condition that can be triggered by flashing lights, flickering screens, or rapidly changing visual patterns. If you are unsure whether you have such a condition, consult your physician BEFORE participating. Symptoms of a seizure include: sudden blackout or loss of consciousness, uncontrolled body movements, visual disturbances (flashing lights, tunnel vision, sudden blackness or visual loss), confusion, muscle stiffness. IF ANY OF THESE OCCUR: the researcher will immediately remove the headset, call for emergency assistance, and contact campus emergency services.
